ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Mary Shelley Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for headaches with episodes of numbness and weakness of the right hand and leg. Concerns: Headaches for about two years, now most mornings, and frightening spells in which her right hand and leg go numb and weak for a few minutes; Afraid of being told it is "only nerves" again, and of losing the use of the hand she writes with; Has lived through many losses and does not want her son burdened; wants to understand everything and decide for herself. [S]

Dexamethasone 4 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice a day for three days before surgery, then tapered and stopped over ten days after surgery

Two tablets up to every 8 hours as needed

tr.td: Resting 12-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm 74/min, normal intervals

MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium, with diffusion imaging and MR angiography of the head and neck: a 3.1 x 2.7 x 2.6 cm extra-axial, dural-based, uniformly enhancing mass on the left frontoparietal convexity over the hand area of the precentral gyrus, with a dural tail and a cerebrospinal fluid cleft; moderate vasogenic edema extending 2.5 cm into the white matter; 2 mm midline shift; no infarct, no other lesion; arteries normal. Appearance typical of a meningioma
Routine EEG with sleep deprivation: intermittent focal slowing and sharp waves over the left central region (C3); no seizure recorded

Left frontoparietal craniotomy with total excision of the convexity meningioma, its dural attachment, and a margin of dura (Simpson grade I), with neuronavigation and motor mapping; dural graft. Pathology: meningothelial meningioma, CNS WHO grade 1 (1 mitosis per 10 high-power fields, no brain invasion, no atypical features; Ki-67 3 percent; no TERT promoter mutation or CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion)
MRI of the brain with gadolinium the day after surgery: gross total resection with no residual enhancement; expected postoperative changes; edema smaller
MRI of the brain with gadolinium three months after surgery: no residual or recurrent tumor; edema resolved; small area of gliosis under the craniotomy

Pneumococcal conjugate PCV20, polysaccharide CRM197 conjugate, adjuvant, PF

Recurrent severe headaches with dizziness, pain in the right hand and eye, transient partial paralysis of the right leg and hand, tremors, and convulsive seizures; called psychosomatic, a derangement of the nerves, and neuralgia by her physicians
Ill health and extreme depression recorded in her journal

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Urgent MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium, with diffusion imaging and MR angiography of the head and neck, within three days; EEG within a week; ECG, blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, and TSH today; headache and episode diary

Safety now: no driving until the cause is known and her seizures are controlled for the period her state requires; showers rather than baths, no swimming alone, and no work at heights; seizure first aid explained; come at once for a longer episode, weakness that does not recover, or a severe sudden headache
Neurosurgery consultation if the MRI shows a structural lesion, to explain the options and their risks to her and plan treatment with her
Grief and mood: a grief history, PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each visit, and the neuro-oncology counselor offered; no assumption that her symptoms are "nerves"
Protect her writing: occupational therapy assessment of hand function if weakness persists, and voice dictation as a backup

Levetiracetam 500 mg twice a day for focal epilepsy due to the meningioma; seizure diary; ask about irritability and low mood at each visit; continue for at least a year after surgery, then decide with her whether to taper after an EEG

Shared decision: resection by craniotomy aiming at Simpson grade I, her choice after observation (not advised for a symptomatic tumor with edema and seizures) and stereotactic radiosurgery (less suitable at 3.1 cm with edema next to the motor cortex) were explained; dexamethasone 4 mg twice a day from three days before surgery, tapered and stopped after it; MRI within 48 hours after surgery

After resection of a CNS WHO grade 1 meningioma (Simpson grade I): no radiation; MRI at three months and then yearly for five years, then every two years; no progestin-containing hormone therapy without discussion
A diagnosis within two weeks, explained in plain words with the images and reports
MRI and EEG within a week; diagnosis explained at two weeks with the images
Full use of the right hand and return to writing every morning
Grip equal on both sides by three months; writing every morning
Decide on treatment herself after hearing the options, benefits, and harms
Chose resection after observation and radiosurgery were explained
Mood and grief supported: PHQ-9 below 5 and a counselor available
PHQ-9 4 at six months; completed eight sessions with the neuro-oncology counselor

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; writing slowed because her right hand tires and twice the pen dropped during an episode [S]
Alert, articulate, and composed; mood "tired and frightened"; affect appropriate; no psychotic features; no thoughts of suicide; speaks of old griefs as long carried rather than new; MoCA 27 [S]
